name: Loeb–Sourirajan cellulose acetate reverse-osmosis membrane
description: At UCLA, Sidney Loeb and Srinivasa Sourirajan developed an asymmetric cellulose acetate membrane that let water pass at usable rates while retaining dissolved salts. A thin selective surface was integral to a thicker porous supporting layer.

date.basis: Loeb recalls a 1959–1960 development window. UCLA’s account gives 1959, and the patent was filed in November 1960.

events.statement: UCLA researchers demonstrated a functional cellulose acetate membrane for reverse-osmosis desalination.

evidence.supports: The inventor dates the development and describes the selective skin and porous support.
Identifies the California research site and corroborates the material and achievement.

date.label: 29 November 1960
date.basis: US patent face records the filing date.

events.statement: Loeb and Sourirajan filed a US patent application for a high-flow desalination membrane.

evidence.supports: Identifies the inventors, application date and cellulose acetate embodiment.

earliest_record.rationale: Loeb’s retrospective gives the earliest evidenced range for the working membrane. The patent preserves a separate documented filing milestone.
